evidence.claim: The White House stated in June 2026 that steel, aluminum and copper imports are covered by strengthened tariff policy, and referenced copper being added to the Section 232 tariff program at the same 50% rate as steel and aluminum.
evidence.source_title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Strengthens Tariffs on Steel, Aluminum, and Copper Imports

evidence.claim: The Bureau of Industry and Security describes 2025 actions applying Section 232 steel and aluminum tariffs to additional derivative products and revoking general approved exclusions and country-level alternative arrangements effective March 12, 2025.
evidence.source_title: Bureau of Industry and Security: Section 232 Steel and Aluminum

evidence.claim: Nucor states that it is North America’s largest and most diversified steel and steel products producer.
Nucor’s annual report says it is North America’s largest recycler, uses scrap steel as the primary raw material, and manufactures steel principally with electric arc furnaces.
Alcoa’s 2025 annual report lists U.S. primary aluminum facilities at Massena West, New York and Warrick, Indiana with stated nameplate capacities.
Freeport-McMoRan’s 2025 annual report describes copper production and includes mines, smelting and refinery assets in its portfolio.
The Department of Defense announced a $150 million loan to MP Materials to add heavy rare-earth separation capabilities at Mountain Pass, California as part of a wider July 2025 agreement.
evidence.source_title: Office of Strategic Capital Announces First Loan Through DoD Agreement With MP Materials to Secure Critical Materials Supply Chain

evidence.claim: MP Materials announced a public-private partnership with the Department of Defense to accelerate an end-to-end U.S. rare-earth magnet supply chain, with expected commissioning of a new facility in 2028 and estimated U.S. rare-earth magnet manufacturing capacity reaching 10,000 metric tons.
evidence.source_title: MP Materials Announces Transformational Public-Private Partnership with the Department of Defense

evidence.claim: Descartes describes customs and regulatory compliance software covering cross-border trade, HS classification productivity, duty spend, CBP compliance and Automated Broker Interface tools.
Descartes’ SEC filing describes applications including classification of goods for tariff and duty purposes, sanctioned-party screening, customs filings and electronic shipment manifest processes.
evidence.source_title: Descartes Systems Group Fiscal 2025 Annual Filing

memory_update.text: NUE is a high-priority domestic steel capacity candidate for the tariff_reshoring_strategic_metals node due to large North American steel and scrap-recycling exposure.
AA is a direct aluminum candidate but requires careful treatment because global supply chain exposure can make tariffs a cost headwind as well as a domestic-capacity tailwind.
FCX is a strategic copper candidate; pure tariff exposure is diluted by global commodity pricing and non-U.S. operations, but supply scarcity and U.S. copper assets support inclusion.
MP is a strong chokepoint candidate for critical minerals and domestic rare-earth magnet reshoring, supported by explicit DoD partnership evidence.
DSGX is a second-order infrastructure/software candidate for tariff complexity via customs, classification and compliance automation.

Potentially relevant but not included due to five-candidate cap: Cleveland-Cliffs for automotive flat-rolled steel, Steel Dynamics for steel/recycling/aluminum ramp, Kaiser Aluminum for fabrication, Expeditors and C.H. Robinson for customs brokerage, and USA Rare Earth if public-market status/liquidity are confirmed.

For this node, separate upstream domestic-capacity beneficiaries from downstream tariff victims; priority evidence should include tariff pass-through, country-of-origin exposure, domestic-content compliance and exemption/derivative-product treatment.

node: Tariff-driven reshoring and strategic metals: steel, aluminum, copper, industrial equipment, autos, semiconductors, critical minerals, pharmaceuticals
summary: Expanded universe around the tariff/reshoring chokepoint points to domestic metals capacity, regulated strategic-materials assets, and tariff-compliance infrastructure. The strongest public-market mappings in this pass are U.S.-exposed steel, aluminum, copper and rare-earth suppliers, plus trade-compliance software that can benefit from rising classification, reporting and tariff-management complexity. Key risk: tariffs can help upstream domestic producers while hurting import-dependent downstream customers; company-level pass-through, input sourcing, exemptions and derivative-product rules must be verified.
